solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maps Congo randomly like this for small dinosaur

indicators.note: done randomly means without set order, so the letters of the two words before it are mixed up

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as anagram fodder
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: An explorer scatters maps of the Congo while hunting a tiny dinosaur.
explanation.walkthrough: COMPSOGNATHUS is the scientific name of a chicken-sized Jurassic dinosaur; the anagram of MAPS CONGO is followed by THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Compsognathus was a small carnivorous theropod of the late Jurassic, among the tiniest dinosaurs known.

clue.text: Training with computers, very good for processing crude petroleum

parts.note: CAT stands for computer-assisted training
cracking is informal British praise meaning excellent

explanation.surface: A computer-based training course is ideal for learning how crude oil is refined.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat cracking is short for catalytic cracking, the refinery process that breaks heavy oil into petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalytic cracking is the refinery operation that splits heavy hydrocarbon molecules in crude oil into lighter fuels.

clue.text: Learns flying with this light plane — on thermals

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order, so the combined letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; joined to the answer it makes anagram fodder
the letters the combined fodder must rearrange into

explanation.surface: A trainee pilot learns to fly in a light aircraft, riding the rising thermals.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: LEARNS plus the answer, rearranged, gives ON THERMALS, so take LEARNS away from those letters to leave the answer. The de Havilland Moth was a classic training biplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moth family of small de Havilland biplanes, such as the Tiger Moth, were famous light aircraft for training pilots.

clue.text: Blitz causing painful sensation round centre of Liverpool

indicators.note: one piece goes round, enclosing, the letter that follows

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, here of the nine-letter city name

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: Bombing raids on Liverpool caused real pain to the heart of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is RAF slang, chiefly British, for a bombing raid as well as for a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: In wartime RAF slang a prang was a heavy bombing attack, which is what a blitz is.

clue.text: One browsing, gaining in confidence about folio

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: becoming more sure of oneself
F is the standard abbreviation for folio

explanation.surface: Someone leafing through a folio grows more confident as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: SURER wraps round F.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfer in the internet sense is someone browsing from web page to web page.

clue.text: Holy book has hint to be solved within grasp (11, two words)

indicators.note: within places the reworked letters inside the word for grasp

parts.note: to grab is to grasp

indicators.note: a puzzle to be solved must be worked out, so the letters need reworking

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A sacred text holds a clue to a mystery, just within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit inside GRAB, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Granth Sahib, or Guru Granth Sahib, is the sacred scripture of the Sikh religion.

clue.text: It was a time of idleness, accepted behaviour with ten relaxing inside

definitions.text: It was a time of idleness

indicators.note: inside puts the loosened letters into the middle of the word for accepted behaviour

parts.note: a norm is the accepted standard of behaviour

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things up, so the letters of the number shift out of order

parts.note: taken as written for anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A holiday period recalled, when ten people lounged about behaving as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was' marks an obsolete word: non-term was the vacation at a university, when no teaching took place.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-term, an obsolete term for vacation, was the period between university terms when students were idle.

clue.text: Hat rim damaged? Jock's may make a twang

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A battered hat rim makes someone wonder whether a Scotsman's twang comes from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot; thairm is a Scots word for gut or catgut, which makes the string of a fiddle or bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Thairm is Scots for catgut, the material of instrument strings that twang when plucked.

clue.text: Powerful two-wheeler difficult daughter's abandoned on field

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so that letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: hard means difficult
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a ley is a field of grassland

explanation.surface: A troublesome daughter rides off on a big motorbike, leaving her family in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the field word after the shortened one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Harley-Davidson, often just a Harley, is a heavy, powerful American motorcycle.

clue.text: What makes the eccentric fret, artless? No crank, certainly

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the following letters go into an odd order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks what makes an eccentric person, naively fretting, no crackpot at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' looks like a word for an odd person, but it is the starting handle of an old car engine; an eccentric is also an engine part.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-starter is the electric motor that starts an engine, replacing the hand crank formerly needed.

clue.text: A group singing hearts out for The Sweet Flag

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out means removed, so the card-suit letter is taken from the word for singers

parts.note: a chorus is a body of singers
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A choir sings its hearts out in praise of a band's flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like it belongs to the singing; sweet flag is a marsh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorus is the botanical genus of the sweet flag, an aromatic iris-like marsh plant also called calamus.

clue.text: Intriguing group in California, not well after a ruin

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
taken as written
to mar is to spoil or ruin
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A plotting clique in California falls sick after a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' looks like it means fascinating; here it means plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: A camarilla is a cabal of secret advisers who scheme around a ruler, a group devoted to intrigue.

clue.text: Part of buckle, e.g. Sam Browne's end piece?

parts.note: Sam is an example of a man, a chap

indicators.note: the end piece of the surname is its final letter only

parts.note: the surname's final letter

explanation.surface: A buckle part, perhaps the tip of a Sam Browne belt.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sam Browne is an army officer's belt with a shoulder strap, so the surface stays on buckles; here Sam is just a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A chape is the metal plate or catch on a buckle by which it is fastened to the strap, and also a scabbard tip.

clue.text: Mail carrier landed up for it in place

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
for means in place of, so one piece replaces two letters of another word

parts.note: lit is the past tense of light, to land or alight
the letters swapped out
a position is a place

explanation.surface: A postman lands, takes his place, and is on his way.
explanation.walkthrough: In POSITION, the IT is replaced by TIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A postilion rode one of the horses drawing a coach, and historically post-boys carried mail on post-horses.

clue.text: Form of riata in leather, typical of steppe-dwellers?

indicators.note: in places the reshaped letters inside the word for leather

parts.note: tan is to make hide into leather; also a leather colour

indicators.note: a new form of a word is a reshaping of it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A lasso of leather, the sort a nomad of the steppes might carry.
explanation.walkthrough: A riata is a lariat or lasso, apt for horsemen; the question mark warns the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatarian means relating to the Tatars, a Turkic people historically living on the Eurasian steppes.

clue.text: Vehicle on end of tail — waits may give you this

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
O is a dictionary abbreviation for on

indicators.note: end of a word is its last letter, taken alone

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A car at the back of a queue makes you wait, which is all you get.
explanation.walkthrough: Waits are bands of Christmas carol singers going door to door, an old British custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol singing is what waits, the traditional street singers at Christmas, perform for householders.

clue.text: What may be shown by fancier fa-la isn't tremolo

definitions.text: What may be shown by fancier

indicators.note: a tremolo wavers and trembles, so the letters quiver out of their order

parts.note: the letters taken as fodder, ignoring hyphen and apostrophe

explanation.surface: A singer's fa-la-la refrain is no fancy tremolo.
explanation.walkthrough: A fancier here is a pigeon fancier, a keeper of show birds, not a fancier singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantails are fancy pigeon breeds with spread fan-shaped tails, exhibited by pigeon breeders at shows.

clue.text: What's sacred to Hindus leaving its source in the Himalaya etc?

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so leaving it drops the opening letter

parts.note: read as orange is: saffron orange is the sacred colour in Hinduism

explanation.surface: Asking what holy Hindu thing rises in the Himalayas, surely the Ganges.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Ganges, whose source is in the Himalaya; instead read 'What's' as ORANGE'S, orange being sacred to Hindus, and drop its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalaya and similar systems are mountain ranges, long chains of peaks; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Rag-and-bone man, last to get central position, plunging straight down

indicators.note: the final letter is moved to the middle of the word, a shift of position

parts.note: Steptoe and Son was a British TV sitcom about a rag-and-bone man, a scrap dealer

explanation.surface: A junk dealer, coming last, moves into the middle of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about a rag-and-bone man, a dealer in household junk. Its last E moves to the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep-to is a nautical term for a shore or bank that drops sharply down into deep water.

clue.text: Tackle rings engineers dipped in solvent liquid

indicators.note: something dipped in a liquid goes inside it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: terts, from tert-, is a solvent named in Chambers; it holds the inserted letters
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Soldiers fix rope rings after soaking them in a cleaning fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: Tackle here means a horse's harness, not football gear or fishing kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrets are the metal rings on a horse's harness through which the reins pass.

clue.text: Whence silk producers emerge, embroidering REGINA

indicators.note: embroidering works threads into fancy patterns, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Silkworms produce thread for embroidering the queen's initials.
explanation.walkthrough: REGINA is Latin for queen, as on coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Graine is the French-derived name for silkworm eggs, from which silkworms hatch.

clue.text: English propeller e.g. on the Broads, device for gauging planetary movement

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a quant is a punting pole used to push barges on the Norfolk Broads

explanation.surface: An English boat's propeller on the Broads doubles as a planetary instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of English rivers and lakes; a quant is the pole for punting a boat there.
explanation.definitionFit: In old astronomy the equant was a point or device used to account for the uneven movement of planets.

clue.text: Mater's mantle round Spain, producing archetypal local dish?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the garment word wraps the country code

parts.note: a palla was a Roman woman's mantle, and mater is Latin for mother
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A mother's shawl wrapped round Spain creates the country's signature meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' refers back to Spain: paella is the classic Spanish dish, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella, the saffron rice dish from Valencia, is the stereotypical food of Spain.

clue.text: Natural amphitheatres created by state of affairs, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound only

parts.note: circs is informal British short for circumstances

explanation.surface: Natural amphitheatres shaped by circumstances, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: Circs, short for circumstances, means the state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cirques are bowl-shaped hollows carved by glaciers on mountainsides, resembling amphitheatres.

clue.text: Mum has added salt with a spicy dish

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
sal is Latin and chemistry shorthand for salt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum has seasoned the curry with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Sal is the Latin word for salt, familiar from sal volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: Masala is a South Asian spice mixture, and also a dish cooked in such spiced sauce.

clue.text: Seamen's clothes and bedding yielding old coppers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ready-made clothing and bedding issued to sailors
second meaning: old slang for police officers

explanation.surface: Sailors' kit and bedding turn up old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests old pennies, but here they are policemen; slop is back slang for police.
explanation.definitionFit: Slops were cheap clothing and bedding supplied to sailors, and slop is old back slang for police.

clue.text: Decorated with distinction that's overdue when it's about waste conveyor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for overdue wraps the waste word

parts.note: late means overdue
urea is the compound that carries nitrogenous waste out of the body in urine

explanation.surface: An honour that comes too late, like a delayed rubbish truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste conveyor' suggests a bin lorry; it means the body's waste-carrying chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Laureate means crowned with laurel as a mark of honour, so distinguished by an award.

clue.text: In love, X scratched, mark in red

indicators.note: scratched means struck out, so the number is removed

parts.note: smitten means struck with love
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A lover's cross is scratched out, leaving a red mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In love' looks like the definition but is the wordplay. Smit is a farming word for the mark of red ochre daubed on a sheep's fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: A smit is an identifying stain or mark, especially the ruddle mark of red ochre put on sheep.

clue.text: Bony girls I fancy, odd ones being ignored

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A man who fancies thin girls, while ignoring the strange ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bony' looks like a description of the girls; it is the definition, relating to a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac means relating to the ilium, the hip bone, so it is an adjective about bone.

clue.text: I look masculine in unit of light or dull brown

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the unit

parts.note: a phot is a unit of illumination
taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look
M is the abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they look manly in either a bright light or a drab brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Philomot is a variant of filemot, from French feuille morte, dead leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Philomot names the dull yellowish-brown colour of a dead leaf.

clue.text: Nursemaid, girl getting in a state

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the name goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York state
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nursemaid's charge gets herself into a real tizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' suggests being upset; the state is New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is a woman employed to look after children, the modern word for a nursemaid.

clue.text: Pineal shaped plant of upland regions

indicators.note: something shaped is given a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A cone-shaped mountain plant, like the pineal gland.
explanation.walkthrough: The pineal gland is named for its pine-cone shape, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a plant native to high mountain areas above the tree line.

clue.text: Part of abdomen cradling hot rubbery bottle, portable (usually large)

indicators.note: cradling means holding within, so the body word goes around the rest

parts.note: the gaster is the swollen rear part of an insect's abdomen, as in ants

indicators.note: something rubbery is flexible and bends out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A tummy clutching a hot-water bottle, carried about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portable' is a noun here, a carried-about radio; the brackets say it is usually a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto-blaster is a large portable radio and cassette player, a boombox.
